label.trigger: extend, collect or from_iter fills a SmallVec beyond its current capacity from an iterator whose size_hint lower bound is smaller than the real item count, for example a filter or a mapped filter over a range, so the loop has to grow the storage through the single-element push.
label.expected_impact: After the push that grows the storage, the loop keeps using its own element count, which is one short. The next batch is written starting at the slot that already holds the pushed element and the length is set from the stale count, so one element per growth step silently disappears (observed [100, 2, 4, 8, 12] instead of seven values); for types with a destructor the overwritten value is also never dropped.

known_counterevidence.note: When the lower bound is exact (slices, vectors, plain ranges) the up-front reservation makes the first batch take every item, the single-element growth branch never runs, and the result is complete; tests with such iterators pass.

label.fix_summary: Increment the loop's own length counter right after the push in the growth branch (len += 1), so the next batch starts after the pushed element and set_len records the true count.
